source_sentence: From 763 to 1253m MD RKB, the interval was drilled with returns to seabed and comprises claystone (based on MWD data).
note: Hordaland Group. Interval printed as 763 - 1253 m; only 1245-1253 m lies inside the task range. No cuttings here: the report says the lithology of this interval is based on MWD logs and drilling parameters.

source_sentence: This interval comprises massive claystone Claystone: greenish grey to dark greenish grey, olive grey, soft to firm, subblocky, non calcareous, rare micropyrite.
note: Hordaland Group. Lithostratigraphy chapter, compiled predominantly from ditch cuttings descriptions (no sample-by-sample list in the report).

source_sentence: This section comprises of claystones Claystone: moderate brown, soft to firm, blocky, non - slightly calcareous, silty, rare micromicaceous, rare micropyritic. Claystone: greenish grey to dark greenish grey, olive grey, soft to firm, subblocky, non calcareous, rare micropyrite.
note: Hordaland Group. Interval printed as 1420 - 1463 m while the group base is given as 1466 m; 1463-1466 m has no description of its own.

source_sentence: This formation comprises claystone and minor tuff Claystone: medium grey - medium dark grey, olive grey, soft - firm, blocky, non calcareous, slightly silty, trace micromicaceous. Tuff: light grey - medium light grey, dark yellowish brown - greyish brown, medium grey, soft - firm, blocky, ...
note: Balder Formation. Tuff is called minor and has no depths of its own, so it is kept as second class.

source_sentence: This section consists of claystone Claystone: medium grey - dark medium grey, olive grey, soft - firm, minor - moderate hard, blocky, slightly silty, non calcareous, trace micromicaceous
note: Sele Formation.

source_sentence: This formation comprises of a main upper claystone section overlying the Heimdal member sandstone's with basal claystone Claystone: medium grey - light olive grey, brownish grey, soft - firm, blocky - subblocky, non calcareous, occasionally silty, rare micromicaceous, ...
note: Lista 1 Formation. The Heimdal sandstone named in the sentence has its own interval (1624 - 1679 m, next row).

source_sentence: This interval consists of a massive sand package Sandstone: clear - translucent quartz, predominantly fine - medium, rare coarse, subangular - subrounded, well sorted, as lose grains, non - locally traces of calcite cement, trace mica, rare - trace glauconite, rare pyrite.
note: Heimdal (member, inside the Lista Formation).

source_sentence: This interval comprises varicoloured claystone. Claystone: varicoloured; very light grey-light grey, medium grey-dark grey, moderate brown, dark green grey, becoming predominantly olive grey-medium dark grey, firm-moderately hard, blocky, non calcareous, slightly silty, ...
note: Lista 2 Formation.

source_sentence: This formation comprises claystone. Claystone: olive grey-medium dark grey, firm to soft, blocky, non-slightly calcareous, rare micropyrite, rare carbonaceous material, rare glauconite, slightly silty
note: Vale Formation.

source_sentence: This formation comprises sandstone and minor limestone stringers Sandstone: clear Quartz, fine - coarse, predominantly medium, subangular - subrounded, moderate sorted, as lose grains, no visible cement, trace glauconite, rare mica. Limestone: white - light grey, soft, subblocky, ...
note: Ty Formation. Limestone named as minor stringers, no depths of its own.

source_sentence: This section comprises claystone with interbedded limestone stringers benches Limestone: white - light grey, locally pinkish grey, soft - firm, locally silty - very fine sandy, subblocky, glauconitic, generally cryptocrystalline Claystone: medium grey - olive grey, minor moderate brown, ...
note: Jorsalfare Formation. Limestone named as interbedded stringers/benches, no depths of its own. Claystone said to grade occasionally to siltstone and to argillaceous limestone.

source_sentence: This formation consists of claystone and limestone stringers with trace of dolomite Claystone: medium grey - medium dark grey, soft - firm, blocky, non - very calcareous locally grading to argillaceous limestone, silty locally very silty grading to siltstone, locally very fine sandy, ...
note: Kyrre Formation. Limestone named as stringers and dolomite as a trace, no depths of their own. The description (second claystone, limestone, dolomite) continues on page 19.

source_sentence: This interval comprises limestone interbedded with claystone Limestone: white - light grey, pale yellow brown, soft - firm, occasionally argillaceous, glauconite, microcrystalline Limestone: light grey - medium light grey, pinkish grey, subblocky - blocky, argillaceous - very argillaceous grading to marl, ...
note: Svarte Formation. Two rocks named without shares; limestone is named first. The second limestone is called argillaceous - very argillaceous grading to marl and the claystone calcareous - very calcareous grading to marl.

source_sentence: This interval comprises claystone and limestone Claystone: medium dark grey - dark grey, soft, blocky - subblocky, occasionally moderate hard, calcareous - very calcareous, locally grading marl, silty, micromicaceous Claystone: brown grey - medium dark grey, soft - firm, blocky - platy, ...
note: Rodby Formation, Cromer Knoll Group (printed as Redby and Radby). Two rocks named without shares; claystone is named first. The limestone description (argillaceous - very argillaceous grading to marl) is on page 20.

source_sentence: This interval comprises mainly claystone. Claystone: brown grey-brown black-olive grey, becoming predominantly brown black, firm to moderately hard, generally blocky-subblocky, occasionally subfissile, slightly silty, non- slightly calcareous, also slightly sandy with traces of micropyrite ...
note: Draupne Formation.

source_sentence: This interval comprises sandstone (Kimmerian turbidites ?) and claystone. Sandstone: medium grey-medium dark grey, clear - translucent quartz, generally very fine-very coarse, predominantly medium-coarse, poorly sorted, friable-moderately hard, very argillaceous/kaolinitic matrix, ...
note: Heather C Formation. Sandstone and claystone named without shares. The sandstone is described with a very argillaceous/kaolinitic matrix and local claystone lamina, so by the word map it is written as Sandstone/Shale; if the matrix words are not counted the class would be Sandstone. Cores 1 and 2 cover 2550.5-2569.37 m of this interval (see core rows).

note: Oseberg Formation. Siltstone called minor, no depths of its own; it is said to be argillaceous - very argillaceous grading to claystone in part.
